page.layout: One printed page, numbered 13 at the head right. Running head at top: "Cap.1. Principum, Dissertatio." Main text in two-column-width body with a small heading in the middle, a short block of marginal notes on the right margin. Below the text: signature "B 3" and catchword "At".

main_text.p: ritate probato. Itá vt non poffit Miltiades non gratus admodùm nobis accedere, quocum fi posterę ætatis Pontifices conferantur, non tàm plebis Christiane Patres, quàm non Pacis filij meritiffimò exiftimari debent. Hæc de primo Attributo Patris.
main_text.head: Bellarminus de Offic.
main_text.p: “ De hoc officio loquitur * Conc. Africanum in Epiftola ad Damafum Papam, cùm S. Damafum appellat Patrem Patrum: & mos, &c. — Pag.25.Tom.1.Conc.Jo. epist.Suppl.
main_text.head: I. ANIMADVERSIO.

p.i: Concilium Africanum aliud Titulum hunc Papæ attribuere; rem verò aliud negare.

main_text.p: VNum Conc. Africanum inscribit Damasum Patrem Patrum: hunc Tu titulum arripis, tanquàm Primatus Pontificis insigne aliquod documentum. At aliud Conc. Africanum (cui ipse Augustinus interfuit) Appellationem ad Romam prohibet. Hoc cùm primum obiectum fuit Stapletono tuo, ipse protinus stomachatus ilicò, & in Sanctissimos Africani Concilij Patres procaciter debacchatus est. Stapleton.Doctr. Prim.Controv.3. q.7.Cusan.qua supra.{i}Huius Concilij Decreta (inquit) pro suo iure temerè sanxiuerunt. Vide, obsecro, quò iam res redijt. Tu ex vno Concilio Africano obtrudis nobis hoc Attributum[Pater Patrum:] Nos ex altero Concilio Africano opponimus vobis non minoris authoritatis iudicium omnium Patrum. In illo titulum videmus sine re; in hoc verò rem ipsam habemus, id est, expressum Concilij Decretum, quo illud, quod Tu stabilire tantoperè cupis, Ius Pontificale abrogatur. Postremò (nam non opus est, in hac quæstione, diutiùs immorari) habemus ipsissimum Papam Damasum Patribus vestris Papis hodiernis aduersantem, qui, {k}In causa Bonasi, negabat iudicium illud sibi competere. Non competere (inquam) non solum nonconuenire.

page.notes: Marginal reference marks i and k are placed as printed; the note marks * and i/k were matched to their notes in the margins. Printed "Pag.25." and "Sect. IX." kept. Possible misreadings: "Miltiades" may be a proper name as printed; "Bonasi" is printed with long s and kept as printed. Words at the end of the page ("Conc." and the catchword "At") are as printed. Note marks in text may be imperfectly read.
